findings.reason: §14's done-when directs the investigation to start from that field and to rule out the other doors from it, so a premise stated backwards is the sentence a node leans on when it decides which launch doors to exclude.
findings.text: §14 states that `dispatch_launch.py` "appends that scheduler shim to a launch's PATH", but `_worker_environment` composes `os.pathsep.join([*directories, *inherited_entries, *declared_entries])` where the scheduler shim directory is inside the leading `directories` block and only the backend's declared search path is appended last (`reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:689`, `:717`); as written a reader concludes an inherited directory outranks the shim, which would make `argv[0] == /usr/bin/srun` say nothing about allocation membership, while the true prepend is exactly what makes "launched from outside the allocation" follow

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — every cited symbol and file resolves (`claim_next_attempt`, `_claim_may_be_reclaimed`, `_retired_attempt_ended`, `admit_once`, `_committed_reload_tree`, `ADMISSION_VERDICT_LOG_MAX_BYTES`, `record_resumption`, `supervised_launch`, the evidence directory, the companion plan), but five "near line" anchors no longer sit near their symbol.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each unbuilt node names a reproducing measure plus declared negative controls that redden a named case: §13 lists 15 cases with 15 controls each keyed to the case it reddens (e.g. "freeing by age fails the launcher-waiting case"), and §14's control (two code stamps that must resolve to different commits) can fail, so neither done-when is an assertion that holds however the code behaves.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §13 requires every gate log under the run directory with a revision header and a bare `EXIT=` last line, and §14 writes `docs/evidence/fragments/a-run-has-one-live-worker/find-the-second-launcher-of-a-figure-finding.html`, a durable repo path in a directory that already holds nine sibling fragments; no node puts evidence in a scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no new symbol, file or comment carries a plan label, stage name or ticket number; the proposed work names mechanisms ("reservation", "session-walk arm", "placed reading") and the `§N` references appear only in the plan document itself, which is their home.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §14 states that the dispatcher "appends" the scheduler shim to a launch's PATH and concludes from `/usr/bin/srun` that the launcher was outside the allocation; the code prepends it, which is what makes the conclusion sound, so the stated mechanism and the conclusion it supports disagree.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §13 is one deliverable (one attempt reservation taken at every relaunch door), §14 is one deliverable (a read-only investigation naming the launching door), and the landed sections each close on a single verdict.
